title: The `totalStaked() == 0` completeness gate that makes `phUSD.setMinter(PHLIMBO_V2, false)` safe is evaluated in forge's local pass, so it constrains pre-broadcast state, not the state the revoke actually lands in
originBasis: Exact fingerprint b57dcb4b… absent. All five ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast family members on the ledger (ea648ec5ea, 3c957109ef, 2212c1c4e8, 5c6d2c9e3b, 2c53e944ca) checked individually: none sits in _phase4e_phlimboV3Cutover and none concerns the totalStaked()==0 gate. Per-control filing is this ledger's established precedent. M-01 2c53e944ca (fix-pending) READ ONLY — not matched, not modified. NEW.
description: Story 076 Concerns §3 and the inline comment at :1785-1790 argue the V2 mint revoke is safe because two facts hold at the moment it executes: `totalStaked == 0` (so `PhlimboV2._claimRewards` early-returns before its BARE, REVERTING `phUSD.mint` at PhlimboV2.sol:495) and `desiredAPYBps == 0` (so a late staker accrues nothing). Both are enforced by statements that forge evaluates during its single LOCAL execution pass, before transaction #1 is dispatched (the ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast property established by run-23 and documented for this suite in the `:verify` npm doc key). Under `--slow --ledger` the actual broadcast runs for minutes across many blocks, and `PhlimboV2.stake` is ungated and — by this story's own deliberate design — unpausable. So the gate at :1779 is a statement about the fork state at signing time; the `setMinter(PHLIMBO_V2, false)` transaction lands later against state the gate never saw. `VerifyPromotionReady` does re-check `v2.totalStaked() == 0` live (:2420), but only AFTER the revoke has already landed — it detects, it does not gate.
impact: A user who stakes into PhlimboV2 during the broadcast window, after Phase 4e's last `migrate` transaction and while V2 still carries a non-zero APY, accrues pending phUSD that V2 can no longer mint once the revoke lands, and their `withdraw` reverts — freezing principal, which is precisely the failure the gate is documented as preventing. The window is empty today and I verified that empirically, not by assumption: `PhlimboV2.desiredAPYBps() == 0`, `phUSDPerSecond() == 0` and `accPhUSDPerShare() == 0` at block 25678182, so no position can accrue pending phUSD and no late staker can either. The finding is the ordering property, and the escalation trigger is concrete: if V2's `desiredAPYBps` is non-zero at cutover time (the script mirrors it live at :1685, so it is not pinned), this becomes a live principal-freeze vector and should be re-weighed as Medium.
evidence: side-effects.json.localPassOrdering; live reads at block 25678182 recorded in side-effects.json.liveChainReads (`desiredAPYBps`, `phUSDPerSecond`, `accPhUSDPerShare` all 0). Ledger lineage disclosed: M-01 `2c53e944ca` (fix-pending) covers the ABSENCE of post-broadcast verification, which story 075 remedied with `VerifyPromotionReady`; this is the distinct residual — a safety GATE whose ordering the verifier cannot restore, because verification after the fact is not gating.
recommendation: Two options, both cheap. (a) Re-order so the revoke can never precede a live check: split `phUSD.setMinter(PHLIMBO_V2, false)` out of Phase 4e into a separate, separately-signed follow-up key run after `promotion-ready:verify` has confirmed `totalStaked() == 0` against live post-broadcast state. (b) Make the revoke self-gating on chain by routing it through a tiny helper that reads `PhlimboV2.totalStaked()` and reverts if non-zero in the same transaction as the `setMinter` call, so the gate and the mutation are atomic. Additionally, add a Phase 0 `require(IPhlimboV2Like(PHLIMBO_V2).desiredAPYBps() == 0)` so the safe case is pinned rather than merely observed, and the script refuses to run in the configuration where this bites.

classification.assetImpact: None at current live state; a late staker's principal freeze IF and ONLY IF the escalation trigger below is met.
attackPath: 1. Broadcast begins. Forge's single LOCAL pass evaluates require(v2.totalStaked() == 0) at :1779 against fork state at signing time, before transaction #1 is dispatched.
2. Under --slow --ledger the real broadcast spans minutes and many blocks. PhlimboV2.stake is ungated and, by this story's deliberate design, unpausable.
3. A user stakes into PhlimboV2 after Phase 4e's last migrate transaction lands.
4. phUSD.setMinter(PHLIMBO_V2, false) lands afterwards, against state the gate never saw.

5. IF V2 carries a non-zero APY, the late staker accrues pending phUSD that V2 can no longer mint; PhlimboV2._claimRewards hits its bare, reverting phUSD.mint (PhlimboV2.sol:495) and withdraw reverts - principal frozen.
VerifyPromotionReady re-reads v2.totalStaked() == 0 live at :2420, but only AFTER the revoke has landed: it detects, it does not gate.
classification.likelihood: Step 5 is VACUOUS TODAY, verified empirically rather than assumed: PhlimboV2.desiredAPYBps == 0, phUSDPerSecond == 0 and accPhUSDPerShare == 0 at block 25678182, so no position - existing or late - can accrue pending phUSD, and steps 1-4 terminate harmlessly.
classification.assumptions: Graded on live chain state as of block 25678182. The safe value is OBSERVED, not PINNED: the script mirrors V2's APY live at :1685 and no Phase 0 require constrains it.
classification.externalRequirements: A user staking into PhlimboV2 inside the broadcast window - unlikely but entirely permissionless.
classification.whyNotMedium: Every path to principal freeze runs through a non-zero V2 APY, read as 0 on chain. Absent that, a late staker exits cleanly. Medium would grade the hypothetical rather than the code as it will execute.

The value is not pinned - the script mirrors it live at :1685 - so the trigger can be armed between now and the Ledger session by any legitimate APY retune. Re-verify PhlimboV2.desiredAPYBps / phUSDPerSecond / accPhUSDPerShare immediately before broadcast; any non-zero reading reopens at Medium.

justification: LOW on today's state. The ordering defect is real and correctly not refuted by run-23's ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast walk-back (that walk-back established atomic pre-dispatch abort when the local pass REVERTS; here the gate PASSES locally and the mutation lands later against unseen state - the converse case, and I independently concur with the sanitizer's C4 screen on this). But its harmful leg is currently empty on three independently-read zero values, so grading it Medium today would be overstatement of a vacuous window.

c4ValidityScreen: No known-invalid class applies. NOT refuted by the run-23 ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast walk-back: that refutation established that a LOCAL-PASS REVERT aborts atomically before dispatch. PR24-04 is the converse — the gate PASSES locally and the mutation lands minutes later under --slow --ledger against state the gate never saw. The atomic-abort property does not constrain post-local-pass state drift. Conditional-but-latent, with the current-state trigger empirically read as 0 rather than assumed.
dedupDecision: KEPT — distinct defect, NOT a restatement of ledger L-03 ea648ec5ea
dedupReasoning: Explicitly adjudicated per rule 3. Both are ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast descendants, but the family is a MECHANISM, not a finding — this ledger already carries five members filed individually (ea648ec5ea, 3c957109ef, 2212c1c4e8, 5c6d2c9e3b, and M-01 2c53e944ca), so per-control filing is the project s own established precedent and collapsing here would be inconsistent with it. Substantively: L-03 concerns a STATUS FLAG written to an off-chain progress file before the event it attests, whose victim is the patch script s own gate. PR24-04 concerns an ON-CHAIN SAFETY GATE (require(v2.totalStaked()==0)) whose victim is a late PhlimboV2 staker whose principal freezes when the setMinter revoke lands. Different artifact, different victim, different impact ceiling (PR24-04 carries a concrete escalation trigger to Medium if V2 desiredAPYBps is non-zero at cutover; L-03 has none). Remediations do not overlap at all: L-03 is fixed by stamping status after broadcast; PR24-04 is fixed by splitting the revoke into a separately-signed post-verify key or by making it atomically self-gating on chain. Fixing L-03 leaves the freeze window untouched. Also distinct from M-01 2c53e944ca, which PR24-04 already discloses: M-01 is the absence of post-broadcast verification and was answered by story 075 s VerifyPromotionReady; PR24-04 is the residual that verification structurally CANNOT answer, because a check that runs after the revoke detects but does not gate.
